patterns.what_worked: The caller census is what made the reading decidable instead of arguable: 64 matched lines (59 real consumer lines) across the tree, of which exactly two consume the RAW return in a way that distinguishes false from nil (classes/rogue.lua:1263 -> rogue_guide.lua:1614 'args.ar_known == false', and diag.lua:506 -> diag.lua:482 'type(known) == "boolean"'). Both files belong to sibling lanes, so reading (a) could not be made behaviour-neutral from inside compat.lua - the answer had to be (b) plus an additive state accessor, which is the pattern the repo already ships for the same problem (api.get_family_spell_id_state, compat-f4 lane). Proving the 'no behaviour change' claim with a paired baseline-vs-current equivalence run (8 client profiles x 4 ids, 150 checks) instead of asserting it is what turned the claim into evidence; the mutation proofs (10/10) then showed every new pin is load-bearing, and the first pass found three pins that were NOT (a substring pin satisfied by the code's own string literals, and two consumer pins that a reworded consumer slipped past).
patterns.what_was_hard: Two traps. First, the obvious textual pins are weaker than they look: 'never nil' and 'not_known' appear in the code half of the section too, so a pin that searched the whole block was satisfied by the implementation, not the documentation - the comment pins now scan comment lines only. Second, the tree was moving under the lane: an early full-harness run showed two red checks in tests/druid_state.lua whose labels did not exist in the file on disk any more, because a druid lane rewrote it mid-run - the failure looked like mine and was not, and believing it would have sent the lane chasing a phantom.
patterns.skill_gap: Pinning a contract across files needs the pin to be about the CONSUMER SHAPE, not the exact text of a file another lane owns, and that tension has no free answer: the current pins read three exact lines in classes/rogue.lua, rogue_guide.lua and diag.lua, so a legitimate rewrite by an owning lane turns this suite red. The pin is the intended signal (the justification for the binary contract changed and must be re-decided), but it is a cross-lane coupling that has to be declared rather than buried - hence HU-15 and the bench artifact's section 6.

escalation.reason: HU-15: the state accessor api.is_spell_known_state is additive and inert today - no caller needs it yet, while the brief said to add a tri-state only where a caller needs it. The operator rules whether it stays (the contract is then complete for the next unknown-hides row) or goes (a small deletion, nothing else in the lane moves).
escalation.recommendation: Keep it: it is the repo's own compat-f4 pattern, it makes the distinction observable without touching a single caller, and it is the difference between 'the comment says unknown' and 'the API says unknown'. Not blocking - the lane is landed and green under either ruling.
